what_was_done: The stored_used floor is gone, reverting the earlier fix's mechanism: _rebuild lost the stored_used parameter and the last-loop-1 max(used, stored_used), and _compute no longer passes _closure_rounds_used(). A loop 1's used is again only the loop-1 passes of earlier runs (plan 3.3 rule 9); the stored closure count cannot move the arbiter because it cannot tell an earlier run's passes from this run's own. _closure_rounds_used survives as rounds_used()'s floor for the closure form only (decision D13). The residual clone case stands as a spec-steward item, outside this unit's files: the used the script was given should ride the run record when the survey hands rounds_used to the script (S3/W2); until then a clone with no or short run records follows the closure's stored verdict through covering() (decision D8). The flawed test test_replay_uses_the_used_the_script_was_given (it never stored summary() after the passes and asserted the floor) is replaced by test_storing_the_summary_moves_nothing.

Same removal as S4R-verdicts-15 (the regression's cause): no stored_used floor in _rebuild or _compute. New test_storing_the_summary_moves_nothing runs the exact regression setup — loop-1 passes with the finding disputed at pass 1 and the arbiter ruling not_defect at pass 3, cap 3 — asserts converged/clean with rounds_used 3 and covering() answered, then stores summary() into the closure as survey-2's checkpoint will and asserts verdict(), summary(), covering() and the replay input (used 0, rule 9) are all unchanged. With a floor re-added the test fails exactly as the check described: the verdict turns blocked/cap with rounds_used 6 and code:a blocking (verified by mutation).

r16 now holds one fix-x-l2-p3 attempt-1 record (the store keeps one record per (run, workflow, subject, name, attempt), so steps_list could never return the byte-identical pair) and its expect.skipped lists the gate-less step once. The two arbitrations are named arbitrate-u-l1 and arbitrate-u-l2 (loops 1 and 2) and keep their positions, which stay the stored path order (arbitrate-u-l1 < arbitrate-u-l2 < fix-...). test_every_case_is_well_formed now refuses a records case that repeats a (run, workflow, subject, name, attempt) identity; every existing case passes it. The case's expected verdicts are unchanged (names are not read by the rebuild), and the whole conformance file passes.

New records case r21-loop-two-without-loop-one: run r1's only loop is loop 2 (no loop 1 before it) holding one clean review whose reviewer marks AC-1 checked; expect failed/no_result with head empty, chain false and passes_used 0. It discriminates the rule-8 branch: with the no-loop-before items mutated from None to [] the case alone fails (the pass turns ok and converges, coverage marked), the other 49 conformance cases still passing (verified by mutation).

The dependency is now stated in the code, the test and this file; the ORDER.md row itself is the orchestrator's to write (rewrite/plans/ is outside this unit's write scope). Facts corrected and recorded: story_unit.acs is the one reader of the ### AC-N headings and skips ``` and ~~~ code fences; verdicts._story_acs imports it inside the function (no module-level cycle); there is no _acs alias and none is needed — the earlier fix report's alias claim was wrong, and nothing references one. test_items_equal_unit_acs guards the pairing and its docstring now tells a story_unit.py builder (survey-2 rewrites it) to keep the fence-skipping acs. For ORDER.md section 4, the row to add: verdicts | P/py/vsdd/state/story_unit.py | acs stays the one AC reader, skipping code fences, and verdicts._story_acs delegates to it (test_items_equal_unit_acs holds the two together) | S4R-verdicts-7.
